issues.detail: The Hebrew text lists three generations: Ladan (לַעְדָּן), his son Ammihud (עַמִּיהוּד), his son Elishama (אֱלִישָׁמָע). The Chinese renders each as 'X人的兒子' (son of X people), which reverses the relationship: it says 'the son of Ladan people, the son of Ammihud people, the son of Elishama people' — implying each is the son of the preceding name, but the Hebrew explicitly states each is the son of the previous person (בְּנוֹ = his son). The Chinese phrasing makes it ambiguous or reversed, and the addition of '人' (people) is not in the Hebrew. This changes the genealogical relationship.
